chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid from Saif ibn 'Amirah from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) say: 'Sacrifice (al-Nahr) is in Mina for three days, so whoever wishes to fast should not fast until the three days have passed; and sacrifice in the provinces (al-AmSar) is for one day, so whoever wishes to fast, he may fast from the morning (of the first day).'

key_terms.بِمِنًى: In Mina (the specific location for Hajj rituals)
key_terms.ثَلاَثَةُ أَيَّامٍ: Three days (referring to the days of Tashriq)
key_terms.مِنَ الْغُدُوِّ: From the morning (of the following day)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting during the days of Hajj sacrifice in Mina versus other cities?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the geographical distinction in the prohibition of fasting during the Days of Tashriq, a ruling derived from the Prophet's practice and codified in Shia jurisprudence. It highlights that while the restriction is absolute for three days in Mina (the site of the primary sacrifice), it is limited to the first day in other regions, allowing fasting to resume from the morning of the second day. This distinction underscores the principle that the sanctity of the sacrificial site imposes stricter temporal constraints on worship compared to general locations.
